questions.stem: What distinguishes a snowflake schema from a star schema?
options: One or more dimension tables are normalised into related sub-dimensions
The fact table is split into several smaller fact tables
A bridge table replaces the fact table
Dimensions are removed entirely
All tables are stored in 6NF
questions.explanation: In a snowflake schema dimension tables are decomposed into related sub-dimensions around a central fact table, reducing redundancy and improving governance.

questions.stem: What is the primary goal of the snowflake schema?
options: Minimising the number of joins in every query
Improving data quality, storage efficiency and reusability, especially for large shared dimensions
Supporting real-time event streaming
Providing a single entry point for cross-fact queries
Storing behaviour alongside data
questions.explanation: The snowflake schema aims to improve data quality, storage efficiency and reusability while preserving dimensional modelling semantics for analytics.

questions.stem: In the snowflake example, into which components might Dim_Customer be split?
options: Fact, Bridge and Dimension
Hub, Link and Satellite
Customer, Demographics, Employment and Geography
Anchor, Knot, Attribute and Tie
Day, Month, Quarter and Year
questions.explanation: Dim_Customer may be split into Customer (core identity), Demographics (age band, income band), Employment (industry, employer category) and Geography (city, region, country).

questions.stem: How does a snowflake schema typically come into being?
options: It is designed from scratch as a 3NF warehouse
It is generated automatically by a BI tool
It is derived from a Data Vault
It begins as a classic star schema whose wide dimensions are normalised over time into sub-dimensions
It is built by denormalising an Inmon EDW
questions.explanation: A snowflake schema typically starts as a classic star schema (Fact + Dimensions), with wide dimension tables normalised into smaller related sub-dimensions over time.

questions.stem: Why is normalising shared dimensions valuable when multiple fact tables such as Loans, Collections and Marketing Campaigns exist?
options: It removes the need for a fact table
It makes every query a single-table read
It allows the fact tables to be merged
It eliminates the need for a Date dimension
It ensures consistency of conformed dimensions across analytical domains
questions.explanation: When several fact tables share the same conformed dimensions, normalisation ensures consistency across analytical domains and clearer conformed hierarchies.

questions.stem: Why are snowflake schemas often paired with a semantic layer or BI modelling tool?
options: To present flattened, business-friendly views that hide the additional joins from analysts
To convert the schema back into a star schema physically
To enforce Third Normal Form on the fact table
To replay events into the dimensions
To store the dimensions as JSON documents
questions.explanation: Because snowflake schemas introduce extra joins and structural depth, a semantic layer abstracts that complexity and presents flattened views to analysts.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as an advantage of the snowflake schema?
options: Reduced duplication
Fewer joins than a star schema
Improved storage efficiency
Clearer conformed hierarchies
Easier management of slowly changing attributes
questions.explanation: Snowflake schemas introduce additional joins compared with a star schema; the advantages are reduced duplication, storage efficiency, conformed hierarchies and easier slowly changing attribute management.

questions.stem: In which situation is the snowflake schema particularly useful?
options: When dimensions are tiny and rarely change
When only one fact table exists
When dimensions are large, frequently updated and shared across many fact tables
When transactional updates must be fast
When queries must avoid all joins
questions.explanation: The snowflake schema is particularly useful when dimensions are large, frequently updated and shared across many fact tables in enterprise-scale environments.

questions.stem: Toward which normal-form principles does the snowflake schema move by partially normalising dimensions?
options: 5NF or 6NF
DKNF
1NF only
2NF or 3NF
BCNF strictly
questions.explanation: The snowflake schema reintroduces partial normalisation into dimensions, moving closer to 2NF or 3NF principles, though its objective remains analytical usability.

questions.stem: Which query is given as an example that analysts can still run in the snowflake loan approval environment?
options: Which officers are linked to fraud rings?
Which loan documents embed customer C101?
What rate was recorded on 20 January?
Which keys are in the Puppini Bridge?
Approval rates by income band and region
questions.explanation: Analysts can still run queries such as approval rates by income band and region, average interest rate by employment category, and total disbursed amount by branch and quarter.
